messages.subject: regression equations for facets
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

My example codes:

DF <- data.frame(group = factor(rep(1:3, each = 100)),
                 weight = c(rnorm(100, 50, 30), rnorm(100, 75, 45),
                            rnorm(100, 60, 25)),
length = c(rnorm(50, 30, 15), rnorm(50, 20, 10),
rnorm(50, 15, 5)))
library('ggplot2')

ggplot(DF, aes(length, weight)) +
facet_wrap(~group, ncol=1) +
geom_point(shape = 1) +
geom_smooth(method=lm,
se=F,
color="RED",
linetype=1,
size=1) +
opts(strip.text.x = theme_text(size = 10, angle = 0))

produces:

I'd like to add regression equation for each group (1, 2 and 3) (please see example attached) in each corresponding facet, but failed.

As always, any suggestion would be much appreciated!

Cheers Trong.

messages.subject: Re: regression equations for facets
messages.body_plain:
>I'd like to add regression equation for each group (1, 2 and 3) (please see example attached) in each corresponding facet, but failed.

Hi Trong, try something like this:

eqnfunc <- function(d) {   # function to fit models and build text equations
  m <- lm(weight~length,data=d)
  c(eqn=paste( "y=",round(m$coefficients[1],1),"+",round(m$coefficients[2],1),"x",sep=""))
}
library(plyr)
labeldata <- ddply(DF,.(group),eqnfunc )  # create data frame with
equation for each group

At this point you can just add, to your original qplot call,

+ geom_text(data=labeldata,aes(x=5,y=2,label=eqn),fontface="Italic")

...which puts the correct model equation in every panel.

Regards,

Ben

messages.subject: Re: Work around for facet error?
messages.body_plain:
On 4/30/2012 5:35 PM, Adam Loveland wrote:
> Thanks very much. So the bug applies to duplicate records, then, not
> duplicate values necessarily? Just making sure. Thanks again.

Yes.  unique() was being called on a data.frame when it shouldn't have
been. The data.frame was an augmented version of the original data
(additional columns for internal ggplot-ish things). So making the
original data have no duplicated rows is sufficient to make the
augmented data also have no duplicated rows and thus make unique() an
effective no-op on that data.frame.

messages.body_plain:
Hi:

The function to use is scale_y_reverse(), but it uses the 'actual' y
limits (i.e., those for which the scale is trained) rather than the
defined y limits. Here's a toy example:

DF <- data.frame(x = rnorm(50), y = rnorm(50, mean = 20, sd = 5))
library('ggplot2')
ggplot(DF, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() + scale_y_reverse()

However, if you try to set an explicit y range and then apply
scale_y_reverse(), it ignores the defined range:

(b <- ggplot(DF, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() + ylim(0, 50))
b + scale_y_reverse()

Perhaps someone can chime in with a way to use scale_y_reverse() on a
scale with a user-defined y-range.

Dennis

There seems to be a strange bug when using position_fill inside of facet_grid. I'm setting x to a factor, and fill to another factor with 2 levels. Then I'm using geom_bar(stat = "bin", position = "fill") and faceting by two more variables. messages.subject: Re: position_fill bug when in facet_grid
messages.body_plain:
Hi:

Actually, there's a facet_grid() bug in the release version of 0.9.0
to which this may be related, whose fix should be in the development
version (but see below). One workaround is to do the prep work outside
of ggplot2; then there is no problem whether you use facet_wrap() or
facet_grid() in your example. The code below uses the count() function
from plyr to get the groupwise frequencies followed by the mutate()
function to produce a new column of proportions by r level for each
combination of the other three variables.

library('plyr')
u <- count(dept.sub, c('Store', 'Repetition', 'Word', 'r'))
u1 <- ddply(u, .(Store, Repetition, Word), mutate,
                       prop = round(freq/sum(freq), 4))
ggplot(u1, aes(x = Store, y = prop, fill = r)) +
        geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
        facet_grid(Repetition ~ Word)
ggplot(u1, aes(x = Store, y = prop, fill = r)) +
        geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
        facet_wrap(Repetition ~ Word)

Using the development version of ggplot2 in a separate R session, I
came up with blank plots in each case (facet_grid() or facet_wrap())
whether I used your code or mine, so at least in the short term, the
code above is a workaround for the problem in 0.9.0. I'm cc-ing
Winston on this since he's mentioned the facet_grid() bug a few times
before in this group and likely understands the code problem much
better than I.

HTH,
Dennis

>   Y=rnorm(30),

> )

> levels(d$Z) <- c("C", "B", "A")
>
> g <- ggplot(d, aes(x=X, y=Y, colour=Z, size=Z))
>
> # order preserved
> g1 <- g + geom_point()
>
> # levels get reordered
> g2 <- g + geom_point(data=d[d$Z != "A", ])

When I plot this, the levels rendered in the legend are C and B; since
the data from A are missing, the A level is silently dropped when the
legend is trained.

> g2 <- g2 + geom_point(data=d[d$Z == "A", ])

Although the factor levels of Z are consistent throughout the data
(sub)sets, your second call to g2 above is adding a new layer to the
existing ggplot object g2, whose legend has silently dropped the A
level. At this point, the legend has to be retrained to accommodate
the new subset, so the default behavior is probably to order
lexicographically. The workaround is to use scale_manual() on each
aesthetic:

g2 + scale_colour_manual(breaks = levels(d$Z), values = c('red',
'blue', 'black')) +
       scale_size_manual(breaks = levels(d$Z), values = c(5, 3, 1))

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: a problem with crossbar (moving to ggplot0.9)
messages.subject_clean: a problem with crossbar (moving to ggplot0.9)
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

I am struggling with the ggplot2_0.9 in order to reuse my previous code. I asked Had for an help and he suggests me to post again my request to the list (trying to provide a reproducible example). Here it is.

Sorry for posting again the question, I try to better explain my problem.

The following code worked perfectly for me on a linux system with ggplot2_0.8.5 on an older R version:

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(ggplot2)

library(MASS)

stat_sum_single <- function(fun, geom="point", colour="red", size=3, ...) {

   stat_summary(fun.y=fun, colour=colour, geom=geom, size=size, ...)

}

stat_sum_crossbar <- function(fun1, fun2, fun3, geom="crossbar", colour="blue", ...) {

   stat_summary(fun.y=fun1, fun.ymin=fun2, fun.ymax=fun3, colour=colour, geom=geom, ...)

}

carsRidotto <- subset(Cars93, Passengers %in% 4:6)

ggp <- qplot(data= carsRidotto, Passengers, Price, geom="point")

ggp2 <- ggp + stat_sum_single(mean, shape=8, size=8)

ggp2 <- ggp2 + stat_sum_single(function(x) quantile(x, 0.1), colour="orange", shape=17, size=7) +

     stat_sum_single(function(x) quantile(x, 0.9), colour="orange", shape=17, size=7)

ggp2 <- ggp2 + stat_sum_crossbar(function(x) quantile(x, 0.5),

                                 function(x) quantile(x, 0.25),

                                         function(x) quantile(x, 0.75),

                                         geom="crossbar", colour="blue", width=0.5)

ggp2

ggp3 <- ggp2 +

stat_quantile(colour="blue", size=1, linetype=2) +

stat_quantile(colour="orange", size=1, linetype="twodash",quantiles=c(0.1, 0.9)) +

stat_smooth(method=lm, se=FALSE, colour="red")

ggp3

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Here you can find the three resulting graphs:

http://stat.unicas.it/downloadStatUnicas/appoggio/fig-ggp.pdf

http://stat.unicas.it/downloadStatUnicas/appoggio/fig-ggp2.pdf

http://stat.unicas.it/downloadStatUnicas/appoggio/fig-ggp3.pdf

and here is my sessionInfo():

http://stat.unicas.it/downloadStatUnicas/appoggio/sessionInfo.txt

Using the last version of ggplot2 on a Mac OsX installation, I have problem with the second plot. Here is my new sessionInfo()

http://stat.unicas.it/downloadStatUnicas/appoggio/sessionInfoNew.txt

In particular here is the resulting "bad" plot:

http://stat.unicas.it/downloadStatUnicas/appoggio/bad-fig-ggp2.pdf

The third plot correctly adds the regression lines to the second plot (I think the problem lies in the stat_sum_crossbar function). Here is the "bad" third plot:

http://stat.unicas.it/downloadStatUnicas/appoggio/bad-fig-ggp3.pdf

Thanks to the help of Brian Diggs, I succeed in reproduce the ggp2 plot using the group aesthetic in the qplot, i.e. as follows:

ggp <- qplot(data= carsRidotto, Passengers, Price, geom="point", group=Passengers)

but using such change I am not more able to reproduce the third plot.

I really appreciate any suggestion.

Ciao,

domenico

messages.body_plain:
Hi Kristoffer,
  you can pull out the centroid of the largest polygon used in representing each country for a solution that would work in other applications. The key here is to convert to SpatialPolygons and then extract the stored coordinates which are calculated as part of the object definition. Example code below.
 - Allan
R 2.15.0 x86_64-pc-mingw32/x64 (64-bit); ggplot2_0.9.0  maptools_0.8-14   sp_0.9-98

library(ggplot2)
library(maptools)

reg <- map_data("world")

P1 <- ggplot(reg, aes(long, lat)) +
    geom_polygon(aes(group = group), show_guide=F)

worldmap <- map('world', fill=TRUE, col="transparent", plot=FALSE)
world_sp <- map2SpatialPolygons(worldmap, IDs=IDs,
    proj4string=CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=wgs84"))
# coordinates pulls out the centroid of
#the largest (area) polygon for a country
world.label <- data.frame(
    country = names(world_sp),
    coordinates(world_sp))
head(world.label)
# plot with labels
P1 + geom_text(aes(X1, X2, label = country), data = world.label)

messages.subject: Re: Finding country centres to annotate map plot
messages.subject_clean: Finding country centres to annotate map plot
messages.body_plain:
It was noted (offline) that the world object pointed to from the package maps is based on 1980s data and has outdated administrative names like USSR.
It is a bit more work but a quick google search suggests you can download updated data from here:
http://www.gadm.org/  or here: http://www.naturalearthdata.com/
After downloading and extracting the 1:110M cultural vectors shapefile from Natural Earth (free for use), you can convert the ESRI Shapefile to a SpatialPolygonsDataFrame and pull centroids and labels into a dataframe as below. For tips on bringing the Natural Earth polygons themselves into ggplot see:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/plotting-polygon-shapefiles
-Allan

library(rgdal)
##assuming shapefile is in your working directory
## 4 files "ne_110m_admin_0_countries" with
## .dbf, .prj, .shp, and .shx extensions
#setwd("your path to shapefile here")
natearth110m <- readOGR(dsn = ".",
    layer =  "ne_110m_admin_0_countries")
natearth.label <- data.frame(
    country = natearth110m$NAME,
    coordinates(natearth110m))
head(natearth.label)

# use base graphics to check out labels
plot(natearth110m)
with(natearth.label, text(X1, X2, country))
# For a guide on using polygon shapefiles in ggplot2 see:
# https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/plotting-polygon-shapefiles

messages.subject: Fulfill publication requirements with ggplot2
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have to produce a simple plot that
should fulfill the requirments of plots for that specific journal,
which are:

"Figures should not normally exceed 8.5 cm wide (single column) or 17.5 cm by 22.5 cm (double column) when printed. The dimensions of figures submitted for scanning must not exceed 20 by 25 cm. Lettering should be in ´sans-serif´ type (Helvetica is preferred) with only the first letter of the first word and of any proper names capitalised. The x-height after reduction should be 1.3-1.7 mm (or 8-10 point in Helvetica). Thus for the reduction of graphs to 30, 40 or 50% of original linear dimensions, the initial x-height of lettering would be 5, 4 or 3 mm (c. 30, 22 and 18 pt) respectively. Proportionately smaller sizes of type, symbols, grid marks and curve thickness should be used for lesser reductions. Symbols and grid marks should be the same respective sizes and, after reduction, curves and axes should not exceed 1.5 pt in thickness unless required for clarity. Lines should not be thinner than 0.5 pt, or they may drop out during printing."

So there are some points which are easy like the sans-serif font.
With ggsave I can set the appropriate width for the plot (e.g. 8.5 cm for single column) but what is the default font size in ggplot2 resp. how can I- set it to 8-10 points (1.3-1.7 mm x-height). How can I ensure that all lines are between 0.5 and 1.5 pt when saved as pdf with a given widht/height?

Thank you for your help,

Best regards,
Johannes

Thanks for your help again! I didn't use Rgdal though (I'm on Mac OS, should've mentioned that), but it worked just as well with readShapePoly from maptools and fortify. Like this:

# shapefile from Natural Earth
x <- readShapePoly("ne_110m_admin_0_countries", proj4string=CRS("+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84 +no_defs"))
map.df = fortify(x, region = "NAME")

Then I could both use it to get centroids (like you described) and to plot the world map with ggplot2.

/ Kristoffer

messages.subject: Re: Fulfill publication requirements with ggplot2
messages.body_plain:
Dear (servus) Johannes,

I'm sure Babtiste, Koshke, Brandon, Hadley and the other experts can
give you better advice but for a start I can give you an example of
one of my graphs since I face exactly the same problems. This is how I
think I solved these problems:

rm(list=ls())

library(proto)
library(grid)
library(reshape)
library(plyr)
library(digest)
library(ggplot2)
library(tools)

setwd("C:\\Users\\mhk\\Documents\\nur.fueR\\ggsave\\")

df.perc.2 <- structure(list(trt = structure(c(1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 3L),
class = "factor", .Label = c("0-1", "1-2", "2-3")),
	resp = c(100, 94.0193416337148, 90.4454585871723,
		100, 97.865467535666, 95.8563947267053),
	group = structure(c(2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 1L), .Label = c("eggs in
worker cells", "eggs in drone cells"), class = "factor"),
	se = c(0, 1.68994661360938, 2.95728999211006,
		0, 0.549126551165786, 0.824844616926236)),
	.Names = c("trt", "resp", "group", "se"), row.names = c(NA, -6L),
class = "data.frame")

ggplot(df.perc.2, aes(y = resp, x = trt, group = group, colour =
group, linetype = group)) +
	scale_colour_manual(values = c("#000000", "#000000")) +
	geom_smooth(aes(ymax = resp + se, ymin = resp - se), data = df.perc.
2, stat = "identity", size = 0.5) +
	opts(legend.position = c(0.3803, 0.31), legend.background =
theme_rect(colour = 0)) +
	opts(legend.key = theme_rect(colour = 0)) +
	opts(legend.key.size = unit(c(0.9, 0.9), "lines")) +
	opts(legend.title = theme_blank()) +
	opts(legend.text = theme_text(size = 9)) +
	opts(panel.grid.major = theme_line(colour = "white", size = 0.5)) +
	scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0.05), name = "age range of eggs
[day]") +
	scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.02, 0), breaks = seq(90, 100, 5),
name = "eggs remaining [%]") +
	opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size = 9, vjust = 0.9),
		axis.text.y = theme_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.9)) +
	opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 11, vjust = 0.61, hjust = 0.6),
		axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.555, vjust = 0.59,
angle = 90)) +
	opts(plot.margin = unit(c(0.3, 0.3, -0.03, -0.23), "lines"))

ggsave("A.plot7.pdf", width = 85/25.4, height = 85/25.4, family =
"sans")

In "geom_smooth" I have added "size = 0.5". In "opts(axis.title.y =
theme_text(.." I have set the size to 11. "opts(plot.margin)", but I'm
sure you use this as well, is extremely useful to make the most out of
a given space. And in the ggsave command you can set the width, hight
and font type.

This graph was produced with the old version of ggplot2. I hope it is
compatible with the new version. Comming back to your questions: I
would always set the font size manually. In this way you know what you
have. I hope the font size I set in the code is the font size in the
PDF. If not this would be a disaster, you're right. I'm curious hear
from the ggplot2 experts about this problem.

On a slightly different note, Hadley and others, would it be possible
in the future to set R in a way that the window presenting the graph
is identical to the PDF? This would save a lot of work and time when
creating a graph. I'm not sure how to do that but (fortunately ;-) I'm
not an expert because I guess this wold be a lot of work.

Best wishes and I hope the example above was useful to you,

Martin

p.s.: Ich bin ebenfalls Österreicher, genauer gesagt Grazer. Wo in
Österreich arbeiten Sie? Es gibt meines Wissens noch nicht viele
Österreicher, die ggplot2 verwenden.

messages.subject: ggplo2 0.9: labeling error when manually dodging discrete scales
messages.subject_clean: ggplo2 0.9: labeling error when manually dodging discrete scales
messages.body_plain:
Hi Group-

I have a continuous y axis, a discrete x-axis, and two discrete
'group' in my data. I want to the plot the groups in the same facet,
and I want to dodge each group a little to the left or right, since
the y values from the two groups are very close together. This worked
just fine in the previous version of ggplot2. However after the 0.9
upgrade whenever I manually dodge the x values, the labels on the x
axis convert to numbers instead of the factor labels.

Here is an example of when it worked in the previous version:
http://dl.dropbox.com/u/9577903/Levels_MarEffectsofInteractions_Loss_reglagz.pdf

Here is example of when it does not work in the current version (note
the x-axis labels have changed):
http://dl.dropbox.com/u/9577903/Levels_MarEffectsofInteractions_Loss_reglagz_stateZs.pdf

I have also tried manually labeling the x axis, but that produces
other unexplainable errors. Below is some sample code for reproducing
the errors and some solutions I've tried.

Any advice on how to get the effect I want without losing the x-axis
labels ( as seen in the first linked pdf above) is appreciated.

Thanks

Here is the example:

library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

#----Create The Data
y<-rep(1:5,2)
y<-y+runif(10,-1,1)
d<-data.frame('yax'=y,'xax'=letters[1:5],mod=c('mod1','mod2'))

#--Create the First Plot
pd<-d
jit<-ifelse(pd$mod=='mod1',as.numeric(pd$xax)-.1,as.numeric(pd$xax)+.
1) #Dodge the points in an ordered way
p1<-ggplot(data=pd,aes(x=xax,y=yax,colour=mod,linetype=mod))
p1<-p1+geom_point(aes(x=jit,y=yax))
p1                                     #X-Axis does not have proper
labels

p2<-p1+scale_x_discrete(name='',labels=levels(pd$xax)) #Produces 'NA's
in the labels
p2

p3<-p1+scale_x_discrete(name='',labels=rep(levels(pd$xax),each=2))
#Shifts the labels to the left
p3

messages.subject: Re: position_fill bug when in facet_grid
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe:

I just retried your original code with the latest development versions
of ggplot2 and scales installed and it works as you expect for both
facet_grid() and facet_wrap(). To install the development versions, do
the following in a fresh R session:

library('devtools')
dev_mode()
install_github('ggplot2')
install_github('scales')
library('ggplot2')

Now run the code of the two plots from your original post. When I did
so, the plots were the same outside of the strip labeling.

Dennis

On Wed, May 2, 2012 at 7:36 PM, Dennis Murphy <djm...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi:
>
> Actually, there's a facet_grid() bug in the release version of 0.9.0
> to which this may be related, whose fix should be in the development
> version (but see below). One workaround is to do the prep work outside
> of ggplot2; then there is no problem whether you use facet_wrap() or
> facet_grid() in your example. The code below uses the count() function
> from plyr to get the groupwise frequencies followed by the mutate()
> function to produce a new column of proportions by r level for each
> combination of the other three variables.
>
> library('plyr')
> u <- count(dept.sub, c('Store', 'Repetition', 'Word', 'r'))
> u1 <- ddply(u, .(Store, Repetition, Word), mutate,
>                       prop = round(freq/sum(freq), 4))
> ggplot(u1, aes(x = Store, y = prop, fill = r)) +
>        geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
>        facet_grid(Repetition ~ Word)
> ggplot(u1, aes(x = Store, y = prop, fill = r)) +
>        geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
>        facet_wrap(Repetition ~ Word)
>
> Using the development version of ggplot2 in a separate R session, I
> came up with blank plots in each case (facet_grid() or facet_wrap())
> whether I used your code or mine, so at least in the short term, the
> code above is a workaround for the problem in 0.9.0. I'm cc-ing
> Winston on this since he's mentioned the facet_grid() bug a few times
> before in this group and likely understands the code problem much
> better than I.
>
> HTH,
> Dennis
>
> On Wed, May 2, 2012 at 4:44 PM, Joe <jofr...@gmail.com> wrote:
>> There seems to be a strange bug when using position_fill inside of
>> facet_grid. I'm setting x to a factor, and fill to another factor with 2
>> levels. Then I'm using geom_bar(stat = "bin", position = "fill") and
>> faceting by two more variables. When using facet_grid(), the fill factor
>> appears to be at 50% in all facets for all levels of x, but by just changing
>> to facet_wrap(), the plot I was expecting come out.
>>
>> Here's an example using data from a package I'm working on:
>>
>> library(ggplot2)
>> library(devtools)
>> install_github("SQAwR", username = "JoFrhwld", branch = "master")
>>
>> library(SQAwR)

>> ggplot(dept.sub, aes(Store, fill = r)) +
>>   geom_bar(position = "fill", stat = "bin") +
>>   facet_grid(Repetition~Word) ## equal areas
>>
>> ggplot(dept.sub, aes(Store, fill = r)) +
>>   geom_bar(position = "fill", stat = "bin") +
>>   facet_wrap(Repetition~Word) ## the expected plot

messages.subject: Re: annotate "rect" in new ggplot2
messages.body_plain:
You can set the limits without clipping the data if you use scale_x_continuous with `oob=rescale_none`:

library(ggplot2)

y <- runif(1000,0.01,50000)
x <- runif(1000,39,810)
df <- data.frame(x,y)

library(scales)
ggplot(df, aes(x=x,y=y))+
  geom_point()+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(100,200,400,800), trans="log",
    limits = range(df$x), oob=rescale_none) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.01,100000), oob = rescale_none) +

  annotate("rect", xmin=0, xmax=10000, ymin=80000, ymax=50000000, fill="blue")

On Tue, Apr 24, 2012 at 7:51 AM, Johannes Radinger <JRad...@gmx.at> wrote:

> Hi,
>
> I just want to reopen an issue we had some weeks ago about extending the plot and drawing rectangles etc. (see correspondence below)
> Therefore Takahashi Kohske helped me by using coord_cartesian.
> This worked for nearly all of my plots but now I realised that there
> is still a little problem with one plot where my x-axis disappeared.
> So I tried to find the problem and found it. Here small
> example to reproduce it:
>
>
> y <- runif(1000,0.01,50000)
> x <- runif(1000,39,810)
> df <- data.frame(x,y)
>
> plot.length <- ggplot(df, aes(x=x,y=y))+
>                geom_point()+
>                scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(100,200,400,800),trans="log")+
>                annotate("rect", xmin=0, xmax=10000, ymin=80000, ymax=50000000, fill="blue")+
>                coord_cartesian(xlim = range(df$x), ylim = c(0.01,100000), wise = TRUE)
>
>
> The problem with the missing x-axis seems to be related to the xlim parameter and the log-scale. Both together don't work in my case. The reason why it worked for my other plots (also with log scale) was related to different xlims. E.g. if I try to set xlim = c(1,810) it works.
>
> Any suggestions how to solve that problem?
>
> Best regards,
> Johannes

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I would like to plot a band of uncertainty based on data
that are produced externally. The data comprise of cumulative
values for the mean (called fit) and a lower and upper bound (lwr, upr).
The problem is that the vectors of lwr, upr and fit are of different
length and they are molten in a dataframe.

A small sample dataset how my data look like:

var <- rep(c("lwr","upr","fit"),c(50,80,45))
y <- c(sort(runif(50,1,20)),sort(runif(80,50,70)),sort(runif(45,20,50)))
x <- c(sort(runif(50,1,100)),sort(runif(80,1,100)),sort(runif(45,1,100)))
df <- data.frame(var,x,y)

ggplot(df,aes(x=x,y=y,colour=var))+geom_line()

It is no problem to plot the three lines (see output of the ggplot command).
But instead of plotting the lines for upr and lwr, I'd like to plot a band/area like the geom_ribbon. I think in this case geom_ribbon wont work...Is there any possiblity to make such a plot? If yes, what is the corresponding ggplot function and how do I need to reshape my data?

best regards,

Johannes

messages.subject_clean: ggplo2 0.9: labeling error when manually dodging discrete scales
messages.body_plain:
On 5/4/2012 10:20 AM, fd wrote:
> Hi Group-
>
> I have a continuous y axis, a discrete x-axis, and two discrete
> 'group' in my data. I want to the plot the groups in the same facet,
> and I want to dodge each group a little to the left or right, since
> the y values from the two groups are very close together. This worked
> just fine in the previous version of ggplot2. However after the 0.9
> upgrade whenever I manually dodge the x values, the labels on the x
> axis convert to numbers instead of the factor labels.
>
> Here is an example of when it worked in the previous version:
> http://dl.dropbox.com/u/9577903/Levels_MarEffectsofInteractions_Loss_reglagz.pdf
>
> Here is example of when it does not work in the current version (note
> the x-axis labels have changed):
> http://dl.dropbox.com/u/9577903/Levels_MarEffectsofInteractions_Loss_reglagz_stateZs.pdf
>
>
> I have also tried manually labeling the x axis, but that produces
> other unexplainable errors. Below is some sample code for reproducing
> the errors and some solutions I've tried.
>
> Any advice on how to get the effect I want without losing the x-axis
> labels ( as seen in the first linked pdf above) is appreciated.
>
> Thanks
>
> Here is the example:
>
> library(ggplot2)
> library(scales)
>
> #----Create The Data
> y<-rep(1:5,2)
> y<-y+runif(10,-1,1)
> d<-data.frame('yax'=y,'xax'=letters[1:5],mod=c('mod1','mod2'))
>
> #--Create the First Plot
> pd<-d
> jit<-ifelse(pd$mod=='mod1',as.numeric(pd$xax)-.1,as.numeric(pd$xax)+.
> 1) #Dodge the points in an ordered way
> p1<-ggplot(data=pd,aes(x=xax,y=yax,colour=mod,linetype=mod))
> p1<-p1+geom_point(aes(x=jit,y=yax))
> p1                                     #X-Axis does not have proper
> labels
>
> p2<-p1+scale_x_discrete(name='',labels=levels(pd$xax)) #Produces 'NA's
> in the labels
> p2
>
> p3<-p1+scale_x_discrete(name='',labels=rep(levels(pd$xax),each=2))
> #Shifts the labels to the left
> p3

I've got three approaches: label the (now) continuous scale with
discrete values, force the scale to be discrete, or let ggplot do the
dodging for you. They are ordered in increasing goodness of approach (in
my opinion).

Labeling the continuous scale:

p1 + scale_x_continuous(name='', breaks=as.numeric(d$xax),
labels=d$xax[d$xax])

Forcing the discrete scale:

ggplot(data = pd, aes(x = xax, y = yax, colour=mod, linetype=mod)) +
   geom_blank() +
   geom_point(aes(x = jit))

Note that it would be better if instead of just assigning to jit in the
global space, you made that a column in pd.

Let ggplot do the dodging:

ggplot(data = pd, aes(x = xax, y = yax, colour=mod, linetype=mod)) +
   geom_point(position=position_dodge(width=0.4))

This doesn't use your jit variable at all.

One way to simplify the problem a bit is to convert the table of
proportions to a data frame, multiply the proportions by 100 and then
pass the result to ggplot2, as Winston suggested. Here's one way:

library('ggplot2')
u <- as.data.frame(prop.table(with(mydf, table(x, g)), 2))
u$Freq <- 100 * u$Freq
names(u) <- c('z', 'group', 'Pct')

ggplot(u, aes(x = z, y = Pct)) +
    geom_histogram(stat = 'identity', fill = 'blue') +
    facet_wrap( ~ group)

HTH,
Dennis

Hi again...

here is an update of my progress:

I used Joran's approach of interpolating (see below).
The plot is now working after some adaptations to my data structure.
There is still a little question concerning the plot (transparency) itself (see at the end).

1) My data frame included also some grouping variables
for facet-plotting. So, first I had to run the interpolation and
creation of the new data frame for upper and lower in
a loop.

2) As my original x data were highly skewed (lot of very small values, fewer
large values) the interpolation failed at the parts of very small values. Thus I used exp(log) in combination with seq to get a log-scaled sequence
for the new x values (and I increased the amount of points)

Here the example of the loop (over species and steps) and the log-scaled sequence:

# Get upper and lower for geom_ribbon
ls = list()
for(j in levels(df$species)){
	for(i in levels(df$step)){
	df1 <- df[(df$species==j  & df$step==i & df$ci!="fit"),]

	r <- range(df1$value)
	xout <- exp(seq(log(r[1]), log(r[2]), length.out=100))
	lower <- with(df1,approx(value[ci=="lwr"],y=abscount[ci=="lwr"],xout=xout,rule=2))$y
	upper <- with(df1,approx(value[ci=="upr"],y=abscount[ci=="upr"],xout=xout,rule=2))$y

	df2 <- data.frame(x=xout,lower=lower,upper=upper,species=j,step=i)
	ls[[paste("ci.df2",j,i,sep="_")]] <- df2
}}
df3 <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, ls))

The resulting dataframe I then used in the ggplot command with facets (grouping variable = steps, facetting = species).

There is just one little question concerning the plot itself and the
transparency. When I use the ggplot-command as mentioned by Joran:

ggplot(df) +
geom_ribbon(data = df1,aes(x = xout,ymin = lower,ymax = upper),alpha = 0.5)
+ geom_line(aes(x=x,y=y,group = var))

...also the line is plotted with the transparency level alpha=0.5. How do
I change that, so that the ribbon is transparent but not the line which plots on top of the ribbon?

Best regards,

Johannes

messages.subject: Re: scientific notation: 10^-8 instead of 10e-08
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I just tried your example...
..I am not quite sure but I think there is a problem
with your example data and the axis. This has to do with
the log scale.

E.g. check your data you created with runif...
most of them are close to 1 and small values
are very very small values are very rare:

Trying your example with:
set.seed(10)

DF <- data.frame(x = runif(1000, 0.00000001, 1),
		y = rnorm(1000))

range(DF$x)

For producing really small numbers one could use:

set.seed(10)
DF <- data.frame(x = exp(runif(1000, log(0.000001), log(1))),
		y = rnorm(1000))
range(DF$x)

Now, plotting either of the two DFs reveals that
the axis does not explain the real extent
of the values. Resp. the range of range(DF$x) and the
range of the axis do not match (of course because the were
transformed before)...

p1 <- ggplot(DF, aes(log(x), y)) + geom_point() +

		scale_x_continuous(breaks = (-6):(-1),labels = math_format(10^.x))

p2 <- ggplot(DF, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() +
		scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0.000001,0.0001,0.01,0.1),labels=math_format(10^.x),trans="log")

So far as I understand ggplot2, one need
to supply the untransformed data and set trans="log,
to get log scaled axis (as in my example before).
Now there is just the question how to get the labels
like I want them...
I'll look that up into the scales package...
Anyway thank you.... :)

/johannes

messages.subject: Re: Rescaling size of points
messages.body_plain:
Stuart,

> Error in continuous_scale("size", "area", area_pal(range), ...) :
>  unused argument(s) (to = c(1, 10))

This error message is actually pretty informative: neither scale_area
nor continuous_scale (to which the former passes data) has a "to"
argument. You probably mean "range=c(1,10)"?

And the legend entries have an "a" in them because geom_text is
contributing to the legend. You could change it to "geom_text(
legend=F, ... )" to get rid of this.

Ben

This may help as well (looks numerical) -

n <- 10

# original demonstration of problem
df <- data.frame(x = 10^runif(n, -19, -13), y = rnorm(n))
qplot(x, y, data = df) + scale_x_log10()

# happens on normal scale, too
qplot(x, y, data = df)

# this helps to see where it happens
u <- runif(n); y <- rnorm(n)
df <- NULL
for(k in 1:18){
  df <- rbind(df, data.frame(x = 10^(-k-u), y = y, g = k))
}

qplot(x, y, data = df) # ok
qplot(x, y, data = df) + scale_x_log10() # ok
qplot(x, y, data = df) + facet_wrap(~ g, scales = 'free_x')
qplot(x, y, data = df) + facet_wrap(~ g, scales = 'free_x') + scale_x_log10()

messages.subject: ggplot2 0.9.1
messages.body_plain:
Should be available from a CRAN mirror near you in the very near
future.  This is mostly a bug fix release, so I'd highly recommend
upgrading from 0.9.0 as soon as possible!

The highlight in this release is a new visual testing system by
Winston, which makes it easier for us to pick up news bugs very very
quickly.

Hadley

ggplot2 0.9.1
----------------------------------------------------------------

MINOR FEATURES

* `ggstructure` and `ggorder`, which call `ggpcp`, no longer have a
  `scale` argument since `ggpcp` does not have one.

* built in datasets have been checked to make sure they use characters,
  factors and ordered factors appropriately

* `geom_raster` and `annotation_raster` gain new `interpolate` argument for
  controlling whether or not rasters are interpolated

* Added `plot` as an alias for `print` for ggplot objects.

* Visual tests have been moved to /visual_test and modified to work with the
  vtest package. (Thanks to Winston Chang)

* `geom_dotplot`: now supports stacking. It uses `stackgroups = TRUE` instead
  of the usual position="stack", for technical reasons. It also will stack in
  the x direction when binning along the y axis. (Thanks to Winston Chang)

* `geom_rug` now allows control over which sides to put the rug lines, with
  the `sides` argument. (Thanks to Winston Chang)

* `annotation_logticks`: a new geom that adds tick marks on the inside of the
  plotting rectangle that have diminishing spacing for log-10 axes. (Thanks
  to Winston Chang)

* Coordinate expansion is now handled by an interaction of the scale and
  coord, rather than by the scale only. Also, the `wise` argument is no
  longer needed. (Thanks to Winston Chang and Kohske Takahashi)

BUG FIXES

* `facet_grid` no longer drops duplicate cases (Fixes #443)

* `munch_range` properly reports the x and y range. (Thanks to Winston Chang)

* `stat_bin2d` handles data with NA in the position variables. Error was
  triggered when scale was limited to a range smaller than the range of
  the data. (Bug reported by Tao Gao; diagnosed and fixed by Brian Diggs)

* `scale_*_identity` will now produce a legend when `guide = "legend"` and no
  breaks or labels are supplied (Fixes #453)

* `geom_map` now works with `coord_map` (Fixes #480)

* discrete scales now accept named vectors of labels again (Fixes #427)

* `geom_raster` works better with categorical input (Fixes #463)

* `qplot` no longer uses non-standard evaluation for geom/stat arguments - it
  doesn't seem to be needed and was causing problems when qplot was used in
  special environments (e.g. in knitr) (Fixes #377)

* `coord_train.polar` and `coord_train.trans` remove NAs from breaks.
  (Thanks to Winston Chang. Fixes #422)

* Theta breaks with `coord_polar` have equal angular spacing. (Thanks to
  Winston Chang and Kohske Takahashi. Fixes #288)

* Empty data frames are now handled correctly: layers with empty data are
  dropped silently, instead of inheriting data from the plot. (Thanks to
  Winston Chang. Fixes #31, #332, #506 and #507)

* The alpha value of set colours is now preserved by default. To return to the
  old behaviour, set `alpha = 1`. (Fixes #475)

* `scale_*_manual` will throw an error if you have too few values. (Fixes
  #512)

* `facet_wrap` gets the `as.table` argument back. (Fixes #497)

* `resolution` now returns 1 when range is zero. (Fixes #526)

* Titles are displayed above legend when legend is on top. (Thanks to
  Kohske Takahashi. Fixes #432)

* Specifying breaks outside coord limits works. (Thanks to Kohske Takahashi.
  Fixes #430)

* `renames_aes` now uses exact matching instead of partial matching. (Thanks
  to Winston Chang. Fixes #529)

* `labs()` now works with American spellings. (Thanks to Winston Chang.
  Fixes #521)

* `stat_density2d` sets the limits for `kde2d` from the limits of the x and
  y scales. (Thanks to Winston Chang)

--
Assistant Professor / Dobelman Family Junior Chair
Department of Statistics / Rice University
http://had.co.nz/

>
> # I want to set the x-axis limits to (-4,4) for facet A and (-100,
> 100) for facet B,
> # and possibly also set manual x-axis breaks independently for each facet

In that case I think you'll have to create separate plots and then
paste them together using the gridExtra package, something like

e <- data.frame(A = rnorm(n=100, mean=0, sd=1),

                 B = rnorm(n=4000, mean=10, sd=40))

a <- ggplot(e, aes(x = A)) + geom_density() + xlim(-4, 4)
# The upper ylim is chosen to approximate equal y-axis
# ticks in the two plots
b <- ggplot(e, aes(x = B)) + geom_density() +
           xlim(-100, 100) + ylim(0, 0.47)

library('gridExtra')
grid.arrange(a, b, nrow = 1)

AFAIK, faceting doesn't give you the level of control over individual
panels that you desire.

Dennis

messages.subject: Bug with scale_fill_gradientn & rescale
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I was just rerunning my code and noticed there have been some changes
in the ggplot2 package. Most notably muted(color) is now available
only through loading the "scales" package and in addition I found a
problem with "rescale" parameter in scale_fill_gradientn. Here's the
reproducible code of an example similar to my code, from
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/scale_gradientn.html :

dsub <- subset(diamonds, x > 5 & x < 6 & y > 5 & y < 6)
dsub$diff <- with(dsub, sqrt(abs(x-y))* sign(x-y))
(d <- qplot(x, y, data=dsub, colour=diff))

max_val <- max(abs(dsub$diff))
values <- seq(-max_val, max_val, length = 11)

d + scale_colour_gradientn(colours = topo.colors(10), values = values,
rescale = FALSE)

This returns an error:

Error in scale$oob(scale$rescaler(x, from = limits)) :
  attempt to apply non-function

So am I to understand rescale is now a function in the new package
"scales". Could anyone be so kind to provide a new syntax of setting
"rescale=FALSE" as in the previous version of ggplot2.

Thanks and much appreciated,

Igor

messages.subject: aligning text in geom_text?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I was wondering if there's a way to align text when using geom_text.
Left-centre-right will do for me but I just couldn't find anything like that in the documentation.

Here's an example that would show where it's necessary (code taken mostly from: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/7201067/showing-variable-labels-under-the-segments-of-dendrogram-with-ggdendro):

library(ggplot2)
library(ggdendro)
data(mtcars)
x <- as.matrix(scale(mtcars))
dd.row <- as.dendrogram(hclust(dist(t(x))))
ddata_x <- dendro_data(dd.row)

p <- ggplot(segment(ddata_x)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x=x, y=y, xend=xend, yend=yend)) +
   scale_y_continuous(trans = 'reverse')
p + geom_text(data=label(ddata_x), aes(label=label, x=x, y=0)) +
  coord_flip()

It would look much nicer if I could align all the labels on the leaves to the left.

Thanks in advance,
Roey

messages.subject: log-scaled colour palette for geom_raster
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I tried the "new" geom_raster for displaying some raster maps (created by GIS). The import and transformation to a dataframe into R and the plot in ggplot2 works really fine and was quite easy to do...so far I am really happy. Now the topic of color-schemes and palettes is really new...

I can get a new color gradient for my raster plot with scale_fill_gradient() resp. scale_fill_gradient() for a more customized way, I that correct so far?

Now I just wanted to know if there is a log-scaled color gradient available or is there any option I can set? My raster maps consists of many very small values and only a few large values and to show differences in the small values, such a log.scaled gradient would be very good. Of course the colors at the ends of the gradient are not important at this time (the gradient is showing probability; range from 10^-8 to 10^-1).

Here a small example with log-data (lots of small, few larger ones):

x <- seq(1,100)
df <- expand.grid(x=x, y=x)
df$z <- exp(runif(10000,log(0.00000001),log(100)))

base <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y, fill = z))
base + geom_raster()

Has anyone done similar things so far and can come up with an example of a nice color-palette/gradient?

best regards,

Johannes

messages.subject: Re: log-scaled colour palette for geom_raster
messages.body_plain:
Hi Brandon,

Problem solved:
I found what i was looking for. One can set
trans="" for the color-gradient. This is really
easy but I thought that transformations are just
for axis but it also worked for the gradient-scales:

+scale_fill_gradient(trans = 'log')

I found that somewhere in the history of this mailing list:
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/5ac9f7d7c8ae7384

Anyway thank you for your help,

Best regards.

/johannes

axis should be fixed which can be done by coord_equal().

p <- qplot(disp, wt, data=mtcars)
p +	geom_smooth()+

messages.subject: Tricky combining of two facets with grid.arrange()
messages.subject_clean: Tricky combining of two facets with grid.arrange()
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'd like to combine two facets created with
ggplot. The first one (p1) has two colums
and one row and x and y axis. The second
plot (p2) has similarly two columns (the same
groups as columns of p1) and three rows.
p2 should be arranged below p1. Thus p2 doesn't
need facet_labels on the x axis (column labels).
Furthermore, p2 doesn't need any axis.text, labels
and ticks in my case. So I removed them via the opts-settings.

When I want to arrange the plots I run into problems,
because of the missing axis of p2. The plots are
not properly arranged... Is there a simple way to
arrange plots by their box?

Here is an example explaining the setup (pls
forget any meaning of the data...it is just to explain
how my plots look like):

p1 <- ggplot(mtcars[mtcars$cyl!=8,], aes(mpg, wt))+
		geom_point()+
		facet_wrap( ~ cyl)

p2 <- ggplot(mtcars[mtcars$cyl!=8,], aes(mpg, wt))+
		geom_point()+
		facet_grid(am ~ cyl)+
		opts(	axis.text.y = theme_blank(),
				axis.text.x = theme_blank(),
				axis.title.y = theme_blank(),
				axis.ticks = theme_blank(),
				#strip.background = theme_blank(),
				strip.text.x = theme_blank())

grid.arrange(arrangeGrob(p1,p2,
			main ="this is a title",
			left = "This is my global Y-axis title"))

Any suggestion and help is mostly welcome.

Best regards,
Johannes
--

messages.subject: Re: 'keep' parameter not working in version 0.9.0
messages.body_plain:
I don't have an answer, but here's a reproducible example that might illustrate the problem (from http://learnr.wordpress.com/2009/05/26/ggplot2-two-or-more-plots-sharing-the-same-legend/):
library("ggplot2")
library("grid")
p <- qplot(data = mtcars, mpg, hp, geom = "point", colour = cyl)
p1 <- p + opts(legend.position = "none")
p2 <- qplot(data = mtcars, wt, disp, geom = "point", colour = cyl) + opts(legend.position = "none")
legend <- p + opts(keep = "legend_box")
Layout <- grid.layout(nrow = 2, ncol = 2, widths = unit(c(2, 0.4), c("null", "null")), heights = unit(c(1, 1), c("null", "null")))
vplayout <- function(...) {
  grid.newpage()
  pushViewport(viewport(layout = Layout))
}
subplot <- function(x, y) viewport(layout.pos.row = x, layout.pos.col = y)
vplayout()
print(p1, vp = subplot(1, 1))
print(p2, vp = subplot(2, 1))
print(legend, vp = subplot(1:2, 2))

Etienne

> 0.9.0:

> Thanks,
> judith

messages.subject: Re: Tricky combining of two facets with grid.arrange()
messages.subject_clean: Tricky combining of two facets with grid.arrange()
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

You don't need both arrangeGrob() and grid.arrange(), one is enough.
The alignment problem is a long-standing, unresolved issue. Kohske has
an experimental branch to solve it that you can try. Other than that,
you'd have to use some hack such as the now defunct align.plots() that
was in ggExtra. I'm not aware of a version that works with facets and
with the most recent ggplot2, unfortunately. You could probably get
some inspiration from this gist and adapt it for multiple panels,

https://gist.github.com/2380653

HTH,

baptiste

messages.body_plain:
Hi All --

I'm trying to get a legend to work with scale_color_identity. I'm failing, and I'm hoping I can be shown the error of my ways.

>From the most relevant docs:
# To get a legend guide, you also need to supply labels, and specify
# guide = "legend"
qplot(1:4, 1:4, fill = colour, geom = "tile") +
  scale_fill_identity("trt", labels = letters[1:4], breaks = colour,
   guide = "legend")

Reproducible example (mostly lifted from the balloonplot docs):

# The data:
carnames <- c("BMW: High End, German",
              "Renault: Medium End, French",
              "Mercedes: High End, German",
              "Seat: Imaginary, Unknown Producer")
carcolors <- c("red","white","grey","green")
datavals <- round(rnorm(16, mean=100, sd=60),1)
data <- data.frame(Car=rep(carnames,4),
                   carColors=rep(carcolors, c(4,4,4,4) ),
                   Value=datavals,  stringsAsFactors=TRUE ) #stringsAsFactors setting specified because my default is FALSE
data$x=sample(1:nrow(data),nrow(data))

# The plots
# just lines
ggplot(data, aes(x=x, y=Value, color=carColors)) + geom_line()

# with assigned colors
ggplot(data, aes(x=x, y=Value, color=carColors)) + geom_line() + scale_color_identity()

# following the scale_fill_identity docs
ggplot(data, aes(x=x, y=Value, color=carColors)) + geom_line() + scale_color_identity("legTitle",labels = 1:nrow(data), breaks=carColors, guide = "legend")
# generates error: Error in is.vector(breaks) : object 'carColors' not found

# following the scale_fill_identity docs, but fully specifying the breaks data
ggplot(data, aes(x=x, y=Value, color=carColors)) + geom_line() + scale_color_identity("legTitle",labels = 1:nrow(data), breaks=data$carColors, guide = "legend") + opts(legend.position = 'left')

All ideas appreciated!

messages.subject: map projections and coord_map and world maps
messages.subject_clean: map projections and coord_map and world maps
messages.body_plain:
The documentation for v0.9.0 says about Map projections, “This is still experimental, and if you have any advice to offer regarding a better (or more correct) way to do this, please let me know.” While not exactly advice, I believe I’ve identified some bugs in coord_map and borders. My question is whether I’m using borders and coord_map incorrectly, or whether borders and coord_map are truly flawed and can be fixed? Below I outline the problems and provide code to produce illustrative examples.

First, artifacts appear on maps when using borders and coord_map. These reflect errors in the polygons that are being created.

library(ggplot2)

library(maps)

p <- ggplot()

p <- p + borders("world", fill = 1)

p   # no artifacts

p + coord_map() #artifacts

These artifacts are worsened when x and y limits are set:

p + coord_map(xlim=c(0,180), ylim=c(0,90))

If xlim and ylim are specified separately, there are fewer errors.

p + coord_map() + xlim(0,180) + ylim(0,90)

All these artifacts are absent if one employs the map function of the maps package to plot the same data, though this precludes using ggplot2 to make complex map overlays, which is my goal.

map(database="world", xlim=c(0,180), ylim=c(0,90))

Second, there is a workaround, using geom_path (rather than borders) to draw the map lines and specifying x and y limits separately from coord_map.

p <- ggplot()

wrld <- map_data("world")

p <- p + geom_path(data=wrld, aes(x=long, y=lat, group = group))

p # no artifacts

#artifacts return using coord_maps x and y limits

p + coord_map(xlim=c(0,180), ylim=c(0,90))

# no  artifacts if x and y limits specified separately

p + coord_map() + xlim(0,180) + ylim(0,90)

However, this workaround precludes the shading of landmasses (since they’re now paths and not polygons). It also precludes some of the map-specific functionality of borders and map_coord, such as interchangeably specifying longitudes with the range -180 to 180 degrees or 0 to 360 degrees; this particular capability is key for a map spanning the antimeridian.

p <- ggplot()

p <- p + borders("world")

p

# specify xlim within coord_map with range 0 to 360 degrees, albeit with artifacts

p + coord_map(xlim=c(100,300), ylim=c(0,90))

# cannot specify xlim separately with range 0 to 360

p + coord_map() + xlim(100,300) + ylim(0,90)

p <- ggplot()

wrld <- map_data("world")

p <- p + geom_path(data=wrld, aes(x=long, y=lat, group = group))

p

# cannot specify xlim separately with range 0 to 360

p + coord_map() + xlim(100, 300) + ylim(0,90)

Again, there is a workaround; one can use the map data “world2”, which has longitudes in the range 0 to 360. Although this also requires that any data to be plotted in another layer also have longitudes in the range 0 to 360 rather than the customary range of -180 to 180. The necessary conversion can be accomplished by adding 360 to longitude values less than 0.

p <- ggplot()

wrld <- map_data("world2")

p <- p + geom_path(data=wrld, aes(x=long, y=lat, group = group))

p # lots of artifacts

# can specify separate xlim using 0 to 360; artifacts now gone

p + coord_map() + xlim(180, 225) + ylim(50,75)

# though artifacts may still appear wth particular limits

messages.subject: Re: plotting longitudinal data
messages.body_plain:
Hi:

You don't make it easy to help, but here's one stab at it.

Caveats:
    (i) You said the exposure levels were 1-4, but you have four
variables whose values are all over 10 also labeled as 'expxx', where
xx is a number.
    (ii) You repeated the same variable name twice.
I just retained the (seven) variables whose values were between 1 and
4, along with the id and gender variables.

Calling the read-in data frame DF, the trick is to melt the data so
that the occasions become a single (factor) variable and their
corresponding values a separate variable named 'value'. The melt()
function is in package reshape2. Next, I used the ddply() function
from the plyr package to get group/occasion means, but there are other
ways to do the same task that returns a data frame. The two resulting
data frames were then used as input to ggplot2 in separate layers.

library('ggplot2')
library('reshape2')
library('plyr')

# Keeps the first 9 variables, using the first two as ID variables
DFm <- melt(DF[, 1:9], id = 1:2)
# Convert gender to factor - use levels() to define M and F
# because you didn't mention it in your post
DFm$gender <- factor(DFm$gender)

# Find the occasion/gender means:
DFmsumm <- ddply(DFm, .(gender, variable), summarise,
                             emean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE))

# Now plot:
ggplot(DFm, aes(x = as.numeric(variable), y = value, colour = gender)) +
    geom_point(size = 3,
                      position = position_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0.2)) +
    geom_line(data = DFmsumm,
                    aes(x = as.numeric(variable), y = emean), size = 1) +
    labs(x = 'Occasion', y = 'Level of violence')

The occasion variable is coerced to numeric so that one is plotting
occasion number; it is also easier to plot lines when the x-variable
is numeric. The points were jittered in both the horizontal and
vertical directions to avoid overplotting.

BTW, this is a preferred way of sending data to an R-related news list
by e-mail:

> dput(DF)
structure(list(id = 1002:1007, gender = c(0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L,
1L), exp01 = c(3L, 4L, 4L, 3L, 3L, 4L), exp02 = c(4L, 2L, 4L,
3L, 2L, 3L), exp03 = c(3L, 3L, 4L, 2L, 1L, 3L), exp04 = c(NA,
2L, 4L, 2L, 3L, 4L), exp05 = c(NA, 3L, 4L, 3L, 3L, NA), exp06 = c(NA,
2L, 4L, 3L, 4L, NA), exp07 = c(NA, 3L, 4L, 3L, 3L, NA), exp08 = c(49L,
43L, 52L, 52L, 51L, NA), exp09 = c(51L, 47L, 53L, 51L, 50L, NA
), exp10 = c(43L, 41L, 63L, 53L, 48L, 53L), exp11 = c(NA, 45L,
61L, 52L, 51L, NA)), .Names = c("id", "gender", "exp01", "exp02",
"exp03", "exp04", "exp05", "exp06", "exp07", "exp08", "exp09",
"exp10", "exp11"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -6L
))

In this form, useRs can copy and paste the output above into their own
R session (assigned to a variable name) and be assured that the data
they see in their sessions are the same as what you have in yours. In
contrast, there is no such guarantee when copying and pasting raw
output. For example, I had to convert gender from numeric to factor;
it is also possible that I may have needed to do that with id had the
occasion arisen. dput() eliminates the need for post-fixes.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Choosing from a subset of point characters
messages.subject_clean: Choosing from a subset of point characters
messages.body_plain:
Hi:

Here's one way to do it:

ggplot ( DF, aes (x = Spec, y = Value)) +
  facet_wrap ( ~ Facet) +
  geom_point ( aes ( shape = Variable, size = 2, colour = Variable)) +
  geom_line ( aes ( group = Variable, linetype = Variable, colour =
 Variable)) +

  scale_shape_manual(breaks = levels(DF$Variable),
                                  values = c(0, 3, 4))

BTW, to get rid of the '2' in the legend, move size = 2 outside the
aes() statement in geom_point(); i.e.,
   geom_point ( aes ( shape = Variable, colour = Variable), size = 2)

In this case, the size aesthetic is *set* to a constant value, so
belongs outside aes(). Variables *mapped* to aesthetics belong inside
aes(), and a legend will be drawn for each such aesthetic.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: breaks and labels in ggplot2 0.9.1
messages.body_plain:
I just upgraded to ggplot2 0.9.1, and I am having problems with breaks and labels.
I am experiencing this problem both in R 2.15.0 under windows 7, and R 2.14.2 under cygwin.
Below is a simple reproducible example to illustrate the issue.
I did not experience this kind of problem in previous versions of ggplot2, including version 0.9.

library(ggplot2)
breaks <- c(10, 20, 30, 40)
ggplot(mpg, aes(x=cty, y=hwy)) + geom_point() + scale_y_log10(breaks = breaks, labels = breaks)
>> Error in scale_labels.continuous(scale, major) :
>>  Breaks and labels are different lengths

It seems that the length of the labels vector has to match the number of breaks shown in the actual plot (not the length of the breaks vector), since the following code works:

library(ggplot2)
breaks <- c(20, 30, 40)
ggplot(mpg, aes(x=cty, y=hwy)) + geom_point() + scale_y_log10(breaks = breaks, labels = breaks)

Is this an intended feature or a new bug?
Is there a general workaround?
Thanks,
Dario

When using log transformation on certain data, the spacing of the labels on the color bar can become a little strange. E.g.

library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)
d <- #A data frame. Note that color has a few values one order of magnitude bigger than the others. Suppose these outliers are of interest.

, x = c(1:50, 1:50)
, color = c(sample(1:10, 10, replace = TRUE), sample(1:10*100, 10)))

A <-
qplot(data = d, x = x, y=y, color = color, geom= "point", size = 2)+
scale_colour_continuous(guide = guide_colorbar(barheight =20), trans ="log10")+
opts(title = "Log10 transform colors")
B <- qplot(data = d, x = x, y=y, color = color, geom= "point", size = 2)+
scale_colour_continuous(guide = guide_colorbar(barheight=20))+
opts(title = "Linear colorscale")
grid.arrange(A,B,ncol = 2)

Is it possible to adjust the rate of change of the colorbar to also be a logarithmic function of it's value?

--
Andrew Winterman

messages.subject: ggmap: Plot within a plot
messages.body_plain:
Hello fellow ggplotters,

I am attempting to create a ggmap plot within a ggmap plot and some on
the finer point of the process are eluding me. The example will
illustrate where I am so far. First, I want to draw an open square on
the mainplot that corresponds to the position of the bounding box of
the subplot. As you can see I have right now manually used a open
square point but this isn't a perfect situation as in subsequent
similar plots I will have to manually place the same point. Can anyone
recommend a way to a) access the coordinates of bounding box in the
subplot and b) plot a square using those coordinates on the mainplot?

In another, not too different matter, I'd like to place a border
around the subplot to better distinguish it on the map. Any
suggestions there?

I really like the develop with ggmap and a big thanks to David Kahle
for all his hard work here.

Thanks in advance!

Sam

Code:

library(ggplot2)
library(ggmap)
library(grid)

###
# Functions
###
full <- function() {
  print(mainplot)
  print(subplot, vp = vp)
}

## Get the maps
map <- get_map(maptype = 'sat', location = c(lon=-121.1356,
lat=52.40725), filename = "big",zoom=10)
lil_map <- get_map(maptype = 'sat', location = c(lon=-121.3817,
lat=52.4708), filename = "lil", zoom=15)

## Set the boundaries
vp <- viewport(width = 0.3, height = 0.3,
               x = 0.97,
               y = 0.66,
               just = c("right","bottom"))

## Make the plots

mainplot <- ggmap(map) +
  labs(x="Longitude",y="Latitude") +
  geom_point(x=-121.3617, y=52.4808, pch=0, size=6,col='white')

subplot <- ggmap(lil_map, extent='device')

## Generate the plots
full()

labs( y="Beginning PD")+
facet_grid( .~end,drop=FALSE,scales="free")

Thanks very much!

messages.subject: Re: combination of stacked area plot and stacked bar plot
messages.subject_clean: combination of stacked area plot and stacked bar plot
messages.body_plain:
Here's what I came up with. It's a little tricky... Instead of using geom_bar, I used geom_area, but to do this I had to do the following:
- Convert discrete xvar values to numeric xvarn
- Make a new data frame by copying the original data, but with new x values at x+0.3 and x-0.3
- The x axis will by default show as numeric, so specify the breaks and labels so it looks like a discrete axis.
- The vertical lines with geom_linerange go from 0 to xvarn, but then they're stacked (like the area plot).

# Set up data

groups <- c("Group1", "Group2", "Group3", "Group1", "Group2", "Group3", "Group1", "Group2", "Group3")

xvar <- c("Var16", "Var16", "Var16", "Var32", "Var32", "Var32", "Var35", "Var35", "Var35")

value <- c(21.1, 13, 5, 39.6, 3.7, 10.4, 21.7, 1, 30)

df <- data.frame(groups, xvar, value)

# Get numeric version of x values
df$xvarn <- as.numeric(df$xvar)

# Make new df with xvarn values shifted to right and left by .3
df2 <- rbind(transform(df, xvarn = xvarn-.3),
             transform(df, xvarn = xvarn+.3))

ggplot(df2, aes(x=xvarn, y=value, fill=groups)) +
  geom_area(colour="black") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymax=xvarn), ymin=0, position="stack") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=1:max(df2$xvarn), labels=levels(df2$xvar))

-Winston

Hi! My issue is related to the creation of manual scales mixing tiled, line, and point layers. I have successfully created manual legends for point and line data in the past, but am getting stuck when adding a gradient into the mix.

The code below generates an example plot. I want the legend to include the gradient scale definition, a line description, and a point description. I did not include my futile attempts to get it working... I am not sure it is possible, so wanted to check before whiling away. There may be a “melt” approach in here, but I don’t see it.

Thanks in advance!

require(ggplot2)

messages.subject: Re: Stat_smooth
messages.body_plain:
But of course!

Say you're working with the mpg data set, you could do something like:

p <- ggplot(mpg, aes(x = cty, y = hwy)) + stat_smooth()

print(p) # To just get the smoother

print(p + geom_point()) # To add the points on top

Alternatively, with qplot()

qplot(cty, hwy, data = mpg) + stat_smooth()

should show both. [Note that for this data set, you might want to
jitter the points a little before use or using  geom_jitter() instead
of geom_point()]

Short answer: yes, just stick +geom_point() on the end of whatever
plotting code you have now.

Hope this helps,

Michael

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for pointing out the aesthetic mapping. Attached is the result I was looking for...almost. I would love less white space between "Surface Contour" and "Observation", but that's just splitting hairs. I had originally hoped to build the legend by stacking scale_colour_manual, scale_linetype_manual, and scale_point_manual, but it seems to get complicated quickly (at least for me).

Sorry, my terminology is probably bad. By "description", I had meant a key,value pair in the legend for the point and line geometries, so yes, my original code would have been confusing.

Appreciate the help! New code is below...

-Ben

require(ggplot2)

## tiled data
tile = expand.grid(x=seq(1,100),y=seq(1,100))
tile$z = tile$x*tile$y

tile$brk = "Surface Contour"

## random "observations" (the points)
obs = tile[sample(seq(1,nrow(tile)),25),c("x","y")]

obs$brk = "Observation"

## construct the plot -----------------------------------------------------------

g = ggplot()
## tile layer
g = g + geom_tile(data=tile,aes(x=x,y=y,fill=z))
## add contours

g = g + stat_contour(data=tile,aes(x=x,y=y,z=z,linetype=brk))
## point layer
g = g + geom_point(data=obs,aes(x=x,y=y,shape=brk))

g$options$labels$fill = "Surface Value"
g$options$labels$linetype = ""
g$options$labels$shape = ""

print(g)

messages.subject: Re: Stat_smooth
messages.body_plain:
Hi:

One way to see what has been plotted is to call the ggplot_build()
function in 0.9.x. For Michael's example, try

p <- ggplot(mpg, aes(x = cty, y = hwy)) + stat_smooth()

ggplot_build(p)

and look at the list element $data[[1]]. I can't guarantee that in
your problem you'll be able to find the corresponding fitted value of
the loess curve at x = 0, in part because the range of your data was
not revealed, but you should be able to extract the prediction at the
maximum x value. By default, geom_smooth() splits the x-range from the
observed data into 80 equally spaced points and returns the predicted
values from loess() at those points (using the default arguments
unless otherwise specified). The information in $data[[1]] is used to
render the smoother with 95% pointwise confidence intervals using the
estimated standard error at each x using a t-based confidence
procedure.

Another approach is to do the loess() fit outside of ggplot2, define a
set of values at which you want predictions and send the corresponding
output into a separate data frame that you can import into the
ggplot() call as separate layers. That would give you more control
over what is plotted, but also requires a little more work on your
part.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Legend with geom_line and geom_smooth using same grouping variable
messages.subject_clean: Legend with geom_line and geom_smooth using same grouping variable
messages.body_plain:
Dear List,

Is it possible to specify different linetypes for geom_line and geom_smooth using the same grouping variable, and have them appear separately in the legend?

The following toy example gets me almost what I want using manual scales, but I would like to integrate the smooth line into the legend as a separate row:

DF <- data.frame(group = factor(rep(1:3, each = 100)),
            weight = c(rnorm(100, 20, 10), rnorm(100, 30, 15), rnorm(100, 15, 10)),
                                 height= c(rnorm(100, 20, 6), rnorm(100, 40, 8), rnorm(100, 60, 5)))

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(DF, aes(x = weight, y=height)) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = group)) +
    geom_smooth(data=subset(DF, group==1), aes(fill=group, linetype=group, size=group, colour=group), method='loess', se=T, show_guide=T) +
    scale_linetype_manual('Legend', breaks = levels(DF$group),
    values = c('solid', 'dashed', 'longdash')) +
    scale_fill_manual(drop=F, 'Legend', breaks = levels(DF$group), values = c('steelblue', NA, NA)) +
    scale_size_manual(drop=F, 'Legend', breaks = levels(DF$group), values = c(1, 0.5, 0.5)) +
    scale_colour_manual(drop=F, 'Legend', breaks = levels(DF$group), values = c('red', 'black', 'black'))

So, I would like the legend to have 4 rows labelled '1', 'Smoothed predictions', '2' and '3'. The row for 'Smoothed predictions' would have a red line and ribbon shading.
I experimented with drop=T in the manual scales but couldn't quite get what I wanted.

Does anyone know if this is possible in ggplot2 0.9.1?

Many thanks in advance for any help or suggestions.

Dave Auty
Postdoctoral research fellow
Université Laval
Wood Research Centre
Québec, QC

messages.subject: Use of grid.layout and recordPlot()
messages.body_plain:
Dear group,

I am trying to use grid.layout to put together some pre-recorded plots (made using the recordPlot()) function.  Here are some questions:

1. I am using the recordPlot() function because I plotted a graph using ggplot2, and manually removed part of the plot using grid.remove() (like in Kohske's dirty hack - http://stackoverflow.com/questions/7410525/align-ggplot2-axes-using-grid).  I couldn't think of another way to save this new plot into an object except by using recordPlot().  Is there another way that is recommended?

2. Once I saved my recorded plots into objects, I'd like to plot each plot on the same grid using grid.layout().  Using the code below results test.png only displaying one of the plots, not all three of the plots as specified.  Any ideas why this is the case and how to fix this?

Thank you in advance for your help!
Kim

set.seed(1410)
dsmall=diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds),100),]
qplot(carat,price,data=dsmall,geom=c("point"))
a=recordPlot()
b=recordPlot()
c=recordPlot()

png("test.png",width=3300,height=2550)
grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(4,2)))
vplayout=function(x,y)
 viewport(layout.pos.row=x,layout.pos.col=y)
print(a,vp=vplayout(1:2,1))
print(b,vp=vplayout(1:2,2))
print(c,vp=vplayout(3:4,1))
dev.off()

messages.subject_clean: Legend with geom_line and geom_smooth using same grouping variable
messages.body_plain:
Hi:

One way to do it is to create and save the plot, extract out the loess
info, do a few simple modifications, concatenate the loess data with
the original data, make a couple of adjustments and do the plot...it's
a little easier than it sounds. The game is to hook in the loess data
with the original. Here's my approach:

DF <- data.frame(group = factor(rep(1:3, each = 100)),
            weight = c(rnorm(100, 20, 10), rnorm(100, 30, 15),
rnorm(100, 15, 10)),
            height= c(rnorm(100, 20, 6), rnorm(100, 40, 8), rnorm(100, 60, 5)))

# Initial plot
# The linetypes aren't really necessary, but they do no harm.
p <- ggplot(DF, aes(x = weight, y=height)) +

       geom_line(aes(linetype = group)) +
       geom_smooth(data = subset(DF, group==1),

                   aes(linetype=group),
                   method='loess', se = TRUE)

## do str(ggplot_build(p)) to see what it returns; the second component of
## $data returns info regarding the loess smooth
d1 <- ggplot_build(p)$data[[2]]
# Keep the height, weight, ymin and ymax variables
d1 <- d1[, 2:5]
# Rename x and y to weight and height
names(d1)[1:2] <- c('weight', 'height')
# Create a group variable with a single value
d1 <- transform(d1, group = 'Smoothed\npredictions')

# Add ymin and ymax variables to DF with NA values
DF <- transform(DF, ymin = NA, ymax = NA)
# Now concatenate DF and d1
DF2 <- rbind(DF, d1)
# Redefine group in the new data frame and set its levels
DF2$group <- factor(DF2$group, levels = c('1',
'Smoothed\npredictions', '2', '3'))

# Revised plot:
ggplot(DF2, aes(x = weight, y = height, linetype = group)) +
    geom_line(aes(color = group, size = group)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = group), alpha = 0.2) +
    scale_linetype_manual('Legend', breaks = levels(DF2$group),
                          values = c('solid', 'solid', 'dashed', 'longdash')) +
    scale_colour_manual('Legend', breaks = levels(DF2$group),
                          values = c('black', 'red', 'black', 'black')) +
    scale_size_manual('Legend', breaks = levels(DF2$group),
                          values = c(0.5, 1, 0.5, 0.5)) +
    scale_fill_manual('Legend', breaks = levels(DF2$group),
                          values = c(NA, 'red', NA, NA))

I used \n in the 'Smoothed predictions' label so that the legend takes
up less horizontal space. If you don't want that, remove the \n in the
two places where it appears.

You could do the same thing with a little more work by fitting a loess
model to the data first and then creating a data frame of predictions,
but ggplot_build() does this more quickly and efficiently so that's
why I did it this way.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Use of grid.layout and recordPlot()
messages.body_plain:
Hi:

recordPlot() isn't going to work with grid graphics, I don't think. I
can confirm that your way doesn't produce three graphs on a page using
grid. I also tried the grid.arrange() function in the gridExtra
package, and that turned out to be illuminating. Note that
recordPlot() comes from the grDevices package in base R.

set.seed(1410)
dsmall=diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds),100),]
qplot(carat,price,data=dsmall,geom=c("point"))
a=recordPlot()
b=recordPlot()
c=recordPlot()

library('grid')

grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(4,2)))
vplayout=function(x,y)
 viewport(layout.pos.row=x,layout.pos.col=y)
print(a,vp=vplayout(1:2,1))
print(b,vp=vplayout(1:2,2))
print(c,vp=vplayout(3:4,1))

As I'm sure you found, this renders one graph at a time, each of which
takes up a complete graphics page. You could say that the graphs are
'grid-unaware'. Trying this with gridExtra,

library('gridExtra')
grid.arrange(a, b, c, ncol = 2)

Error in arrangeGrob(..., as.table = as.table, clip = clip, main = main,  :
  input must be grobs!
...which tells you that the output of recordPlot() does not yield
grobs that the grid package can recognize.

OTOH, if you do

a <- qplot(carat,price,data=dsmall,geom=c("point"))
b <- qplot(carat,price,data=dsmall,geom=c("point"))
c <- qplot(carat,price,data=dsmall,geom=c("point"))

and use the code above, both will print as expected because a ggplot
graphic is a grob (graphical object). It seems that what you need is a
way to edit/modify your plots in order to return grobs with which the
grid package can work. Perhaps the grid experts on this list can
provide more specific details.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Use of grid.layout and recordPlot()
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

recordPlot records the displaylist, which I think is valid for both
base and grid graphics. However, its print method has no extra
argument, let alone a viewport,

getS3method("print","recordedplot")

Insted, I would suggest recording the modified ggplots as grobs, e.g.
with grid::grid.grabExpr or grid.grab. These can be redrawn in
specific viewports with either grid.arrange or grid.draw.

HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: when to use geom_rect(ymin=-Inf, ymax=Inf)
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I'm trying to add a background band to a faceted plot with free
scales, and I'd just like to confirm whether using geom_rect(ymin=-
Inf, ymax=Inf) is the correct behavior.

Example code:

library(ggplot2)

## example data.frame
dates <- as.Date(paste(seq(1860,1870),'-01-01',sep=''))

d <- data.frame(
                year=rep(dates,2),
                facet.by <http://facet.by>=c(rep('a',11),rep('b',11)),
                value=c(rnorm(11),rnorm(11)*100)
                )

## recessions
recession <- data.frame(
                        start=as.Date('1865-01-01'),
                        end=as.Date('1867-01-01')
                        )

p <- ggplot(d, aes(year, value)) + geom_line()

p <- p + facet_wrap(~facet.by <http://facet.by>, scales='free', ncol=1)

p + geom_rect(aes(xmin=start, xmax=end, ymin=-Inf, ymax=Inf, x=NULL,
                  y=NULL), data=recession, fill='grey80', alpha=0.5)

This works as I expected to, but I'd just like to know whether there
are any pitfalls in setting ymin=-Inf and ymax=Inf. (an alternative
I've seen is to set them to the max and min of the dataset, but then
the panels end up having the same scales, I guess because they each
have a geom_rect with the same size).

Best regards,

Alexander

messages.subject: Re: overlapping layer, with different data
messages.body_plain:
Hi:

 In ggplot2, if you define x and y a particular way in ggplot(), it is
expected that those variables will be used for x and y in *all*
subsequent layers, which is why you couldn't get the contours to plot.
The workaround is not to define those variables in the ggplot()
statement but to assign them in the geom calls instead (see
geom_path(), geom_point() and geom_text() below).

Here's one way to get what you asked for, but I don't think it's what
you expected....

ggplot(dta) +
   theme_bw() +

   geom_rect(xmin = 0.0, xmax = 1.0, ymin = 0.0, ymax = yymax,
             fill = 'yellow', alpha = 0.015) +
   geom_rect(xmin = 0.0, xmax = 0.4, ymin = 1.0, ymax = yymax,
             fill = 'red', alpha = 0.015) +
   geom_rect(xmin = 0.4, xmax = 1.0, ymin = 1.0, ymax = 0.0,
             fill = 'green', alpha = 0.035) +
   geom_rect(xmin = 0.0, xmax = 0.2, ymin = F40.F20,
             ymax = yymax, fill = 'red', alpha = 0.15) +

   geom_path(aes(x = SB/v[3], y = Ft/v[1]), linetype = 2, size = 0.3) +
   geom_point(aes(x = SB/v[3], y = Ft/v[1], size = yr, fill = yr), shape = 21) +

   scale_size(range=c(0,5)) +
   labs(y = 'Mortalidad por pesca, relativa a F40%',
        x = 'Fracción de la Biomasa Virginal',
        colour = 'Año', size = 'Año', fill = 'Año') +
   scale_fill_gradient(limits=c(dta$yr[1], dta$yr[length(dta$yr)]),

                       low="black", high="#FF9326") + # colour = yr
   geom_text(data = head(dta, 1), aes(x = SB/v[3], y = Ft/v[1]),

             label = dta$yr[1], colour = 'black',

             vjust = 2, size = 3) +
   geom_contour(data = tmp.3, aes(x = x, y = y, z = z)) +

   scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1)) +
   scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,yymax),
                      breaks = round(sort(c(0.5,1.0,F40.F20,1+(F40.F20-1)/2,
                                        yymax-(yymax-F40.F20)/2)),digits = 3),
                      labels = c(' 0.5','1.0',
                                 paste(round(1+(F40.F20-1)/2,digits=2)),
                                       expression(F[20]/F[40]),

paste(round(yymax-(yymax-F40.F20)/2,digits=2))))

That little splotch of blue around the 2010 point is your contour
plot. You can zoom in on it with coord_cartesian(), but I needed to
get rid of the scale_continuous() calls in order to do that.

One thing you could do would be to create the contour plot separately,
absent the legend and titles, save it at a suitable size, and then use
annotation_raster() or annotation_custom() to insert it into the main
plot as an inset. If you wanted, you could create a small rectangle
around the 2010 point to indicate the position of the contour in the
main plot, perhaps with a line pointing to it from the inset using
geom_segment() with an optional arrow. A couple of examples using
annotation_raster() and annotation_custom() are in the 0.9.0
transition guide:
http://cloud.github.com/downloads/hadley/ggplot2/guide-col.pdf  See
section 4.

HTH,
Dennis

Hi Trong,

Here is a modification of your example including all the features you mentioned.

# DATA
DF <- data.frame(group = factor(rep(1:3, each = 100)),
                 weight1 = c(rnorm(50, 30, 15), rnorm(50, 20, 10),
rnorm(50, 15, 5)),
weight2 = c(rnorm(100, 50, 30), rnorm(100, 75, 45),
                            rnorm(100, 60, 25)))

DF$ID <- 1:nrow(DF)
library(plyr)
library(reshape2)
#MELT DATA
md <- melt(DF, id=(c("group", "ID")))

md.sum <- ddply(md, c("group", "variable"), summarize, value =
mean(value), min = min(value), max = max(value))

#DRAW CHART
require(ggplot2)
ggplot(md,
       aes(variable,
           value)) +
  facet_wrap(~group,
             ncol=1) +
  theme_bw() +

  geom_point (aes(shape = variable,

                  colour=variable),
              size = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(group=variable,
                linetype = variable,
                colour=variable)) +
  scale_shape_manual(breaks = levels(md$variable),

                     values = c(1, 2, 3)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = ID)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1),
            data = md.sum,
            color = "red") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = min,
                    ymax = max),
                width = 0.2,
                data = md.sum,
                color = "red")

The key the this approach is to use different data for the points and
summarized statistics.

Best,
Ista

I'm still new to ggplot but have grown to love it in the past 6 months. Using sample code from from the "choropleth challenge" to help me come up with a solution, I was generating maps from live data to create a series of images for a "time lapse" display. >From the example Hadley provided to the challenge a few years ago: https://gist.github.com/233134#file_polygons.r you can see what I'm experiencing after fixing the "pal" to "palette" and setting a group of unemployment rates to zero (like unemp$rate[unemp$rate <5 ] = 0 prior to the choropleth assignment).

I'm reading about the new geom_map and looking at revisiting the code but is there a simple way to get similar scaling from 0.8.9?

messages.subject: Package for using system fonts in R graphics
messages.subject_clean: Package for using system fonts in R graphics
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone -

I'm working on a package that makes it easy to use use different fonts in PDF output:
  https://github.com/wch/extrafont

Currently it supports only Truetype fonts. This seems to be the most commonly used format on Mac, Windows, and Linux.

It has two external dependencies:
- Ghostscript
- ttf2pt1, a program for extracting/converting afm (font metric) files from ttf files

There are a few things I'd like to do:
1. Remove the dependency on ttf2pt1 by including the source for tt2fpt1 and compiling it on installation.
2. Make sure it works properly on Windows. The only version of Windows that I've tested it on is Windows XP.
3. Add support for Postscript fonts.
4. Make sure it works for Eastern (CJK) fonts.

If you can help with these things -- especially 1 and 2 -- it would be greatly appreciated.

I've attached an example of the output (generated on Ubuntu 12.04) so that you can see that it really works. This is the code used:

setupPdfFonts()

pdf("fonttest.pdf")
qplot(1:5, 1:5) + xlab("Made with extrafont package") +
  opts(axis.title.x=theme_text(size=14, family="Purisa"))
dev.off()

embedExtraFonts("fonttest.pdf")

-Winston

1		2					3			1
1		2					5			1
2		1					4			4

:		:					:			:

What would be the cleanest way to do this via ggplot2? Any tips would be greatly appreciated. I will continue to monkey with ggplot2 while I see if anyone has some brilliant ideas.

thanks!

Ani
